items.problem: The handling of a `security` line written after a window has ended and before the job `logging_security_flush` has deleted it is not set. Line 98 starts a new window only for a group key and `reason` that "have no window", and counts only the lines "in the window", while line 99 deletes an ended window only when the job runs, which can be up to a period later. Run path: a window starts at t, the last job run started just before t, and a second line of the same group key and `reason` is written at t + `logging.securityRepeatWindowMs` before the next job run ends. One implementation counts that line in the old window, and another writes it as the first line of a new window, which then exists together with the ended window. The line count and the summary `count` differ between them. This existed before the diff, which only sets the range of the key

The behavior of the job `logging_analytics_deletion` when the current environment has no analytics adapter and rows remain is not set. Line 175 skips writing a row only at request time, line 164 allows `environments.<ENV>.adapters.analytics` to be `null`, and line 177 sets the job unconditionally and calls `delete_user_data` of the adapter for each row. Run path: rows are written under `analytics-ga4`, the game setting is then changed to `null` and the server restarts. The table has scope `game`, so the rows remain. One implementation throws, another skips and keeps the rows, and another counts failed attempts until the row is deleted. The test at line 289 covers only an environment without an adapter that leaves no row

`logging.analyticsSendTimeoutMs` has no written range, so the default rule at skills/core/SKILL.md:134 allows 0. It is an external service time limit, which skills/server-core/modules/server-time.md:89 measures only with `network_time_limit`, and that operation throws for ms less than 1 (skills/server-core/modules/server-time.md:39). Input: game settings `core` with `logging.analyticsSendTimeoutMs` 0 passes the schema check, and then every `send` and `delete_user_data` call throws instead of ending with one of the failure kinds of line 170. `push.sendTimeoutMs` (skills/server-core/modules/push.md:195) writes `1 or more` for the same case. The diff sets the range of the two job period keys and does not touch this key

`logging.analyticsDeletionMaxAttempts` has no written range, so the default rule at skills/core/SKILL.md:134 allows 0, and its result is not settled. The meaning is the max number of times one deletion request is sent, while lines 177 and 178 send the request before comparing, and the incremented `attempts` of 1 never equals 0. Input: value 0 with a failing `delete_user_data`. One implementation sends once and deletes the row, another sends without end because `attempts` never reaches the value, and the meaning says it is never sent. `storage.userChangeRetryMaxAttempts` (skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:365) writes `1 or more` for the same kind of key

The order of the analytics consent check and the name check of line 109 in `ReportAnalyticsEvents` is not set. Line 106 places the consent check only "after the limit check", and the limits of line 108 are entry count, event count, param count and string length, not the name rule. Input: a user with `analytics_allowed` `false` or no row sends an event named `core_x`. One implementation returns `INVALID_REQUEST`, another succeeds with an empty response and `consent_dropped_count` 1. The tests at skills/server-core/modules/logging.md:284 and logging.md:287 each cover only one of the two conditions.

A settings value that passes every check makes core requests fail. Lines 132 to 134 apply `logging.maxStringLength` and `logging.maxEventParams` to `track_core_event`, and a violation throws and ends the request with `INTERNAL`. Neither key has a range that keeps the core analytics event table valid: skills/core/SKILL.md:134 and SKILL.md:135 allow any value of 1 or more for the first and 0 or more for the second, and skills/client-core/modules/log-core.md:157 and log-core.md:158 only bound the `LogCore` keys by them. Input: game settings `core` with `logging.maxStringLength` 16: `core_session_started` (20 characters) throws in step 6 of `auth` (skills/server-core/modules/auth.md:146), so every login of a user with `analytics_allowed` `true` is `INTERNAL`. With `logging.maxEventParams` 4, `core_iap_granted` (5 params) throws in the grant.

The input of the adapter operation `send(events)` is not set. No line defines the fields of an element, and the two saved forms differ: `logging_client_event` has `received_at` and `logging_server_event` has `request_id`, and both hold `params` as bytes. Line 165 needs the user ID, `name`, `params` and `time_at` from it. skills/server-core/modules/testing.md:144 returns this value from `calls()`, and the test at logging.md:281 says the fake adapter receives "the saved events as they are", so its assert differs per implementation. It is also not set whether two `track` calls in one transaction make one `send` with two events or two `send` calls with one event each.

The behavior of a split `send` is not set. Line 165 splits more than 25 events over several calls, and lines 169 and 170 define one time limit and one failure for `send`. Input: 60 events (when `logging.maxEvents` allows them) where the first call fails. One implementation stops and loses 35 events, another sends the rest, and the failure kind of a mix of results is not set. `logging.analyticsSendTimeoutMs` (line 240) says "an analytics adapter call", so it can be read as the limit of each HTTP call or of the whole `send`, while skills/server-core/SKILL.md:206 requires a total time limit of an external service call.

`truncate_ip` (skills/server-core/modules/logging.md:30) does not set the handling of an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address or the text form of its output. skills/server-core/SKILL.md:243 makes the server listen on all addresses, and skills/server-core/modules/routing.md:171 takes the client IP from the peer address of the TCP connection, which a dual-stack listener can report as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`. Keeping the first 48 bits of that value gives `::` for every IPv4 client, so all unauthenticated IPv4 clients share one group key at logging.md:98, and the `security` line of a second client with the same `reason` is not written. Another implementation treats it as IPv4 and keeps 24 bits. The text form (`2001:db8:1::` or the full form) decides the duplicate check of `ips` at logging.md:99 and is not set either.

The rule for `after_seq` 0 differs from skills/server-core/modules/admin-api.md:176. Line 126 and the row at logging.md:221 make an `after_seq` less than 1 `bad_request`. The body rules, which collected operations follow (admin-api.md:111), say `after_seq` is 0 or more and that 0 means from the start of the range. Input: `list_client_events` with `after_seq` 0, with or without `after_time_at` and `after_user_id`. One implementation returns the range from its start, another returns `bad_request`.

The result of `log` with a level that is not one of the four is not set. Line 47 lists the levels, the API row at line 28 has failure value `none`, and the `## error` table has no row for it. Input: a content handler calls `log` with level `trace`. One implementation writes a line with that level, another drops it, and another throws and ends the request with `INTERNAL`.

The failure path of the job `logging_analytics_deletion` does not set the case where the row no longer exists. Line 179 says two server instances may send the same row at the same time, and line 178 increments `attempts` "the same way" in one `storage.run_game_transaction` and, at `logging.analyticsDeletionMaxAttempts`, deletes the row and writes an `error` log. Run path: instance A succeeds and deletes the row, instance B's call fails and then increments `attempts` of the missing row. One implementation upserts the row back with `attempts` 1 and requests the deletion again, another updates no row; when the increment would reach the max, one writes the `error` log for a row already deleted, another writes nothing
